commentary:
📚 Three months into writing her first draft, she realised she was trying to write 20 books in one.

That's what Kylie Paatsch, one of our EAC authors, shared on the Entrepreneur to Author podcast with Scott MacMillan recently.

She was lost. Confused. Didn't know what she wanted to say anymore.

So she stopped. Let the draft sit for two months. Came back to it... and wrote it so much faster.

Because by then, she was clear.

This is the part about writing that nobody warns you about: it doesn't just capture your thinking, it changes it.

Kylie's Know-Show-Grow framework — for helping senior leaders develop the leaders they lead — was already good before she wrote the book. Now? It's bigger. Sharper. She can articulate it at a level she couldn't before.

That's what writing does to your work.

📕 The Connect Effect by Kylie Paatsch is a practical guide for senior leaders on building loyalty, ownership, and engagement with the leaders under them. Published by EAC Books.

Her advice for anyone sitting on a book idea: stop waiting for the perfect moment and just start. Writing will deepen your framework, strengthen your voice, and grow your impact.

🎧 Listen to the full conversation: https://lnkd.in/gVjFGn9w

📚 Get The Connect Effect: https://lnkd.in/gvTkNgPh

author: urn:li:organization:89798536
commentary:
Lately, people arrive to write a book with more material than ever.

Reams of notes. AI-generated outlines that run for pages. Ideas, drafts, and possibilities... if you can even find the one that matters.

The hard part is no longer producing words.

It's knowing what to trust. What to keep. What to cut...

What actually serves the reader, and what just sounds like everyone else.

Nowadays, that kind of judgment is what "real work" is.

We're writing into a very different world than even a year or two ago. And there are very few places that help us build the discernment, clarity, and stronger decision-making that good writing actually requires.

That's the work we care most about. It's what we've been shaping Intake 5 to be... a stronger environment for thoughtful, human, trusted writing.

If there's a real book in your work, this might be the room to develop it well.

Applications for early enrolment are open until 23 June.

media.title: 6 Books on the Personal and Human

commentary:
Surviving a 5% chance. Mothering through the mess. Healing through story. Building community one verge garden at a time.

6 books from our @[Expert Author Community](urn:li:organization:89798536) authors that won't sit on your business shelf.

📕 Mostly Ups by @[Kerryn Harvey](urn:li:person:MYAzuGQY6A)
Survived necrotising fasciitis with a 5% chance of living. Lost her arm. Then competed for Australia and ran 12 marathons in 12 months.

📗 Seen Again by @[Benita Bensch](urn:li:person:xPMpsz43Dc)
A real and refreshing perspective on the emotional complexity of family life - the tension between caring for your children and staying connected to yourself.

📘 The Perfect Parent Trap by @[Lisa Taylor](urn:li:person:fUUf9k3VWJ)
A therapist's guide to building relationships that help us feel loved, grounded, and genuinely connected.

📕 Welcome Home by @[Bee Lim, Ph.D.](urn:li:person:amzST1vLnh)
Through four animals, psychology, and storytelling - a beautifully illustrated work grounded in healing and human experience.

📗 Between Flights by @[Wendy Walker](urn:li:person:uRJEzzK2CW)
Written in the pauses between airports, meetings, and milestones - reflections on leadership, life, and the unseen moments that shape us.

📘 Garden on the Verge by @[Gayle Dallaston](urn:li:person:HMScYHgjra)
The case for native verge gardens as one of the simplest ways to increase community connection. Local action creating hope.

📚 28 books from our community in 2026. Read the full list here: https://lnkd.in/gAgY\_xY8

5 books from our @[Expert Author Community](urn:li:organization:89798536) authors that ask the questions most performance books skip.

📕 Win the Night to Win the Day by @[Penelope Barr](urn:li:person:blo2KB7FPJ)
Reframes sleep as the most overlooked strategic tool we have. For anyone tired of leaving their best days to chance.

📗 The Cognitive Athlete by @[Clint Rahe](urn:li:person:jwDKJ6smo0)
Drawing on elite sport, military, and neuroscience - a practical guide to building focus and mental strength under pressure without burning out.

📘 The Overachiever's Reset by @[Fleur Marks](urn:li:person:p2rI9vBufo)
A deeply honest guide to succeeding differently, with more sustainability and self-trust. Permission to reset without giving up.

📕 Why Things Feel F\*cked by @[Andrew Sloan](urn:li:person:yhmnUlxeIy)
Blending psychology, storytelling, and practical insight - a grounded path back to self-leadership, meaning, and lasting change.

📗 It's Not You, It's Perimenopause by @[Sarah Gray GAICD](urn:li:person:Q7KUC1Ke47)
A nutritionist and pharmacist brings clinical expertise and genuine warmth to navigating the hormonal, physical, and emotional changes of midlife.

📚 28 books from our community in 2026. Read the full list here: https://lnkd.in/gAgY\_xY8

commentary:
There's a disco ball at a bookshop in Melbourne tonight...

And honestly, that tells you everything you need to know about Fleur Marks.

Fleur is launching her book The Overachiever's Reset at Readings Emporium tonight. Drinks. Books. Sparkle. A room full of people who get it.

But here's the thing.

Behind the disco ball is a story most people wouldn't put on paper.

The woman who had it all. Nearly lost herself getting it. Survived cancer. And then sat down and wrote - with brutal honesty - about what happens when the "having it all" model breaks. What it actually takes to succeed without losing yourself in the process.

That's not a self-help pitch. That's a life.

And she turned it into a book.

📚 The Overachiever's Reset is for anyone who's ever wondered whether the pace they're keeping is the pace they actually want. It's honest, it's real, and it's the kind of book that makes you stop scrolling and start thinking.

Tonight, Donna McGeorge MCs the launch at Readings Emporium - Level 1, 287 Lonsdale Street, Melbourne.

If you're in Melbourne, be in the room. You'll be glad you were.

If you're not, drop Fleur a congratulations below. Share this. Grab the book. These moments matter.

CONGRATULATIONS FLEUR 🪩 

Get the book here: https://lnkd.in/gRdKNiWY
RSVP to fleur\@fleurmarks.com.au

author: urn:li:organization:89798536
commentary:
"I think this is crap. I'm going to give up."

That is what EAC author @[Lisa Taylor](urn:li:person:fUUf9k3VWJ) said to her mentor @[Michelle Scheibner](urn:li:person:\_grOLvKTUE) during the 18 months it took to write The Perfect Parent Trap.

Not once. Multiple times.

And Michelle would say: "No, you're not. You're going to do this."

This was not a rehearsed anecdote from a polished stage moment. This was the real, unfiltered truth of what writing a book actually looks like.

Sticky notes on the kitchen bench. Late nights. Her husband Larry thinking the notes she left around the house were love letters - when they were actually ideas she had during the day.

Here is what Lisa taught everyone in the room at her launch in Geelong:

It is not about feeling ready or confident. It is about having someone beside you who will not let you quit when the doubt gets loud.

Lisa did not finish her book because she suddenly believed in herself. She finished because she had a mentor who believed in the work - even on the days Lisa could not.

And somewhere inside all that mess, she discovered something she never expected.

"I actually love writing. I can't believe I'm saying that."

She laughed when she said it. But it landed.

Because the book you keep telling yourself is not good enough might be the one that matters most.

The moments where you want to quit are often the moments right before something shifts.

📚 Congratulations Lisa Taylor on bringing The Perfect Parent Trap into the world.

author: urn:li:organization:89798536
commentary:
Community building must be in-built into every step of your book. 📚

After an incredible 90 minutes with community expert, legend, and yes, EAC Advisor, @[Paz Pisarski 🏵](urn:li:person:ZCaRi4JRpd) from @[The Community Collective](urn:li:organization:75023406) yesterday, one thing became crystal clear: the worst time to tell people about your book is when you're launching it.

Successful authors co-create WITH their readers throughout the entire process.

They:
• NOTICE - Identify the specific problem you're solving 
• NICHE - Be niche cubed \(three specific traits, not just general "coaches"\) 
• ENGAGE - Ask what challenges, support, and goals your readers have 
• SHARE - Present solutions back, showing how you've actioned feedback

To all of the aspiring authors out there:
Stop asking "How am I going to launch this book?" Start asking "Who can help me?"

As Paz says: "The worst thing you can do these days is do anything alone."

To the Expert Author Community members who joined us - thank you for making this session so rich with your questions and insights.

What's your biggest community building challenge as an author?

--

📚 Want your book to be backed by a community that sees the big picture and cares about every step? 

We'd love to talk to you: https://lnkd.in/g5naNZdQ

author: urn:li:organization:89798536
commentary:
Yesterday inside the EAC, we hosted a special session with five powerhouse authors from our community:

@[Melo Calarco](urn:li:person:UOGZjWFsIr), @[Tony Frost](urn:li:person:\_Y2MZWe1T\_), @[Anna Glynn \(MAPP\)](urn:li:person:\_755VWVqKt), @[Donna McGeorge](urn:li:person:wzpTbgXWG3), and @[Sarah Martin \(Kinchington\)](urn:li:person:xqqALNAKMY).

Their honesty, creativity, and generosity sparked an incredible conversation around real-world book marketing - not the kind you read in a textbook, but the kind that comes from doing the hard, heart-led work.


📚 Here are just a few golden insights they shared:

• Build your people before you need them. Donna’s “Red Brickers” helped pre-sell her book with exclusive content and early access.

• Include your book in your speaking fee. Don’t sell from the back of the room - sell from the start.

• Relationships matter. A conversation on a golf course led Sarah to a leading psychiatry professor and a global book ripple.

• Be brave, be bold. Anna’s billboard campaign turned heads and sparked selfies.

• Measure what matters. Lives changed \> sales charts.

• Be strategically shameless. Tony wove his book into conversations with purpose - and no apologies.

• Focus on placement, not presence. Local bookstore relationships often beat airport shelves \(serious\).


💬 If you came to the session, what’s one takeaway you’re sitting on? Drop it in the comments or tag someone writing who needs to hear it.

To our brilliant authors - thank you for leading with both head and heart. You’re showing us all what’s possible.

They’ve had it in their head for months, sometimes years.

But then the writing starts.

The idea sharpens.
The real message emerges.

And suddenly? That original title doesn’t quite fit.

One sentence. At a time.

Every line stands alone - until the very last stage, when it finally becomes a paragraph.

👉 End with a word that lingers

Ever been told “you can’t help the way you feel”?
Total myth.

Your viewpoint → shapes your emotions → drives your actions.
Which means the way you choose to see things literally changes the way you write, lead, and show up.

This is exactly the kind of shift Derek Sivers sparked in our recent 📚 book coaching sessions inside the Expert Author Community. When you realise your state of mind drives your momentum, your book goes from “stalled draft” to “future bestseller.” ⭐

What state of mind helps you take your best actions? 👇

author: urn:li:organization:89798536
commentary:
It’s not always about asking yourself ❤️ “What do I love doing?”

The real question is:
👉 “What do I hate not doing? What leaves me feeling 😒 and deeply unsatisfied if I skip it?”

That’s where the real magic happens — the work that’s worth doing, and the writing that feels impossible not to share.

Inside the Expert Author Community 📚, we see this shift all the time. Authors stop chasing what looks shiny, and start writing the ideas they can’t not put into the world. That’s what fuels books that resonate, sell, and last. ⭐

So tell us — what’s the thing you’d feel icky ignoring in your own work? 👇

author: urn:li:organization:89798536
commentary:
You don’t always need more advice. Sometimes, you just need to sit down and write.

That’s the idea behind our monthly Cowriting Sessions inside the @[Expert Author Community](urn:li:organization:89798536).

These aren’t teaching sessions. There’s no prep required. No pressure to perform. Just you, your book, and a quiet room of fellow authors who are also putting in the work.

Here’s how it works:
 📝 You join the session inside our Circle space 
 🎯 Share a simple writing goal at the start, something you want to make progress on
 🔕 Turn off distractions and write for 50 minutes straight
 ✅ Check back in at the end, reflect, and move on with your day

It’s the gentlest form of accountability, and one of the most powerful.

✨ Some members use it to chip away at a chapter.
 ✨ Others refine a section of their proposal.
 ✨ Many show up just to re-enter the writing rhythm after a long pause.

What they all say afterwards:
 “That was the most productive hour I’ve had in weeks.”

Cowriting Sessions are one of the hidden gems of the EAC, and they’re one reason our members don’t just start writing. They keep writing.

📅 Intake 4 kicks off July 25.
 📬 If you’re craving structured support and flexible writing space—this is it.

media.title: Find the fun in writing again ✨

commentary:
Writing shouldn’t feel like a chore.

Too many people sit down and start writing to some made-up version of who they think they need to impress.

Here’s the truth:
✨ Your voice is enough.
✨ Writing is a skill - and you can learn it.
✨ And yes, it can actually be fun \(especially with the right people around you\).

So ditch the corporate mask. Ditch the pressure.

Write like yourself - and enjoy the process again.

media.title: Still figuring it out? Start the book anyway 📚

commentary:
You don’t have to be the expert before you write the book.

You BECOME the expert by writing it.

“I didn’t know I was the expert in meetings... until I wrote the book on it.”

📚 The truth is...

Most authors in our community don’t start with perfect clarity. 

They start with curiosity, lived experience, and a little spark of “I want to say something about this.”

Sometimes it’s ego. Sometimes it’s FOMO.

But most of the time - it’s because they know there’s more they want to explore, own, or create.

And that’s enough.

Most people think they need clarity or need to be "ready" before they start writing.

When you get started. 

When you put pen to paper.

If you’re serious about being known for something - start messy.

You don’t really need permission. Just a place to begin.

commentary:
✨ We wrapped up Intake 3 of the Expert Author Community in true EAC style: with celebration, reflection, and a surprise visit from two very special guests—Kelly’s parents! 💛

This session was more than a wrap party—it was a moment to pause and honour 94 writers from around the world who committed to one bold, shared mission: write the book only they can write, and positively impact the world while doing it.

🌏 From Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France, Singapore, Switzerland, and the UK, to the US and Canada—this intake was proof that when you write in community, everything shifts.

💬 When asked what surprised them most, members said:
 • Lifelong friends 🤝
 • Confidence they didn’t know they had
 • Trusted travel companions for the creative road ahead
 • Courage to see themselves as real writers
 • The power of perspective, feedback, and momentum

🎉 Here’s what else we celebrated:
 • 134 co-writing sessions \(our highest ever!\)
 • 33 proposals submitted \(double last round!\)
 • A record-breaking Pitch Party with 9 publishing pros
 • And members signing publishing contracts—huge congrats to them all!

🌟 And yes, we got a little teary when talking about the pride of each of our members journeys and progress they’ve made this intake. 

🥂To all of our Intake 3 members—whether behind the scenes or front and centre—thank you. This intake reminded us that writing doesn’t have to be lonely. It can be energising, expansive, even fun.

💫 If you’ve ever wondered whether your book idea belongs somewhere—it does. 

💛 If you’d like to join us for the next round of writing, co-creating, and celebrating—add your name to the EOI list and be part of the next Wrap Party. https://lnkd.in/g5naNZdQ

💡 Use pauses strategically to gather your thoughts
💡 Don’t try to solve everything in one pitch

commentary:
BTS: Navigating the Publishing Landscape with @[Lou Johnson](urn:li:person:7Qdr-4BjMG) & @[Kelly Irving](urn:li:person:YObSNviyfy)

Ever feel like publishing is a bit of a mystery? 

Spoiler: You're not alone! 

It’s one of the reasons our founder and head book coach, @[Kelly Irving](urn:li:person:YObSNviyfy), sat down with one of our Industry Coaches, @[Lou Johnson](urn:li:person:7Qdr-4BjMG), publishing powerhouse and founder of Key People Literary Management, for an in-depth session on publishing commercials, contracts, and the current landscape.

With 30+ years in publishing, Lou has worked with some of the biggest names and books in the industry & has seen it all—traditional, hybrid, and self-publishing. 

Together, she and Kelly held an unfiltered discussion exclusive to EAC members on current market trends, unpacking the key differences between publishing pathways, answered questions on challenges, highlighted opportunities, debunked myths, and answered burning questions from our incredible community on the publishing landscape.

Key Takeaways from the Session:
✅ Publishing isn’t one-size-fits-all – understanding your goals will help determine the best pathway \(traditional, hybrid, or self-publishing\).
✅ Know your rights! Who owns the IP? What’s in the fine print? Contracts matter more than you think.
✅ Follow the money on which publishing pathway will commercially be right for you and your bottom line.
✅ A book deal isn’t just about bookstores – think beyond shelf space. Airports, bulk sales, corporate sponsorships, and speaking engagements can all play a role.
✅ Long-tail strategy matters – your book can keep working for you long after launch day.

💬 What our members had to say:
👉 “This session really clarified my instinct on my publishing path. I feel settled now!” – @[Kristine Posthumus](urn:li:person:FXSOA6Cfb6)
👉 “So valuable as usual—thanks, Lou and Kelly!” – @[Nina Witenden](urn:li:person:F2Teks3W6i)
👉 “I learned heaps! Thanks for your insights.” – @[Catia Davim](urn:li:person:cGyuujeQYs)

author: urn:li:organization:89798536
commentary:
You never really know what goes on behind the scenes of a book 🌟

Today was our final Open Book Coaching session for this intake - and it was a cracker!

We talked so much about our individual journeys and what we've learned over the last 6 months, and there were certainly some common themes in our breakout rooms:

✅ That this journey is SO much more, and more rich and rewarding, than simply just "writing a book"
✅ That we need to redefine measures of success from "how much we have written" to "how much we have learned and applied"
✅ That timelines and deadlines will shift and change according to the above, so it's integral that you realise:

🌟 Writing your book means you are building your business AND your FUTURE 🌟

With our founder Book Coach @[Kelly Irving](urn:li:person:YObSNviyfy) zooming in from her hotel in Dubai this morning \(kids asleep in the background\), it was also a timely reminder that you never know what is really happening behind the scenes of a book \(or a business\)

Respect to all the authors out there! You are all amazing!

We are so excited for our special finale event, our Pitch Party, with special guests from across the industry of publishing! Will you join our next one in Intake 3?

author: urn:li:organization:89798536
commentary:
⭐Yes, people will judge your book by its cover 📙

We cannot stress how incredibly important your book cover is if you want to sell books. 

A cover can really make or break you \(we’ve seen plenty of books disregarded in book awards simply because their cover didn’t hold up, no matter how good the content may have been.\)

So in our latest Guest Expert session at the @[Expert Author Community](urn:li:organization:89798536), we had the award-winning book designer @[Tess McCabe](urn:li:person:ZnMZUXlXWt) share how to make your book move through a killer cover design. 

We explored…
🔸 Why investing in the cover of your book is so important
🔸 The key elements that make a book cover speak to its intended audience.
🔸 How book cover design works in the context of business or personal branding
🔸 How you can find a good designer
🔸 How to provide a killer brief for a designer

Some of our favourite takeaways were: 
⭐ Think about where you see your book fitting into the marketplace. What is your unique point of view?
⭐ Trends matter when it comes to attracting the right readers - know what’s new, what’s been done before and what is coming up
⭐ Align your cover design with your personal brand and business visual identity to make it cohesive and instantly recognisable

What were some of your favourite takeaways?

🌿 Did you know that spending time outdoors could be the secret to unlocking your creative potential?

📚EAC member and Alumni Mentor, @[Dr Jenny Brockis](urn:li:person:jhMUbdR\_nt), dives deep into this idea in her latest book, The Natural Advantage, revealing how even a brief walk in nature can spark fresh thinking. 

🌳A 20-minute stroll or simply surrounding yourself with green spaces, time in nature can help you get your creativity soaring! 

In her recent SmartCompany article, Jenny shares the below key takeaways: 
💡 Time outdoors reduces stress and restores focus, creating the perfect environment for innovative ideas. 
💡 Nature helps broaden your perspective and unlock new ways of thinking. 
💡 A quick dose of sunshine and greenery could be the game-changer when you’re feeling stuck.

🍃As authors, thinkers, and creators, we’re always searching for new sources of inspiration—sometimes, it’s as simple as stepping outside. 

Ready to explore how nature can give your creativity a boost?

commentary:
We had an absolute blast today at Open Book Coaching! 😁 

We ran a role-play pitching exercise where we got to talk about our books, and our book buyers had to make the VERY difficult decision on whether they would put the books on their front counter. 

🌟 The point of the exercise was NOT to be perfect, or to necessarily have a polished pitch \(or even a published book in their hands\).

Instead, together we collaboratively shared our takeaways, what worked well and what things we thought we’d like to know more about. 

Together, we developed a list of what makes a great pitch and how best to prepare for a conversation about your book to ANY potential customer, publisher, book seller or individual. 

📗 This will now form a resource that will be distributed to our members and implemented in our Write Book curriculum.

✅ It’s sessions like these that are the heart and soul of our community, where everyone gets the opportunity to step up and have a say, and we also collaborate and come up with resources for the good of ALL of our members.

What is the @[Expert Author Community](urn:li:organization:89798536) Book Launch?

At the heart of the @[Expert Author Community](urn:li:organization:89798536) lies a powerful ritual - our Community Book Launch. 

This is where we come together to celebrate the incredible achievements of our authors, recognizing not just their finished works but the dedication, creativity, and perseverance behind each book.

The Community Book Launch is more than just a standard book launch \(even though we love book launches of all types!\). 

It’s a platform where authors showcase each other’s work, offering fresh perspectives on topics that matter and positively help the world. 

Our upcoming launch features three diverse, thought-provoking books:
📕 @[Monique Zytnik](urn:li:person:T\_jsgYndaL) – Internal Communication in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
📙 @[Dr Shyam Barr](urn:li:person:2c68J1zAy8) – Educate to Self-Regulate: Empowering Learners for Lifelong Success
📗 @[Dr Jenny Brockis](urn:li:person:jhMUbdR\_nt) – The Natural Advantage: How more time outside reduces stress, improves health & boosts social connection

The event also includes an open Q&A session where attendees can ask these authors about their journey—from the initial idea to the final published book. It’s an opportunity to gain firsthand insights into the challenges and triumphs of writing, publishing, and launching a successful book.

For the Expert Author Community, this launch represents the culmination of months of hard work, collaboration, and mutual support. 

It’s a chance to highlight the incredible depth of talent within our network and a celebration of the power of community-driven success.

The Community Book Launch is a core part of who we are—a living testament to the strength, diversity, and talent of the authors we support.

Here's some amazing insights from Taural's session: 

📌 Set a specific, quantifiable goal
📌 Know the value of your business from the customer \(brand, referrals, joy, etc\)
📌 High value services do not come at the lower price point of the market
📌 Group your clients into 3 buckets: keep, try to keep, let them go
